name: Ramp
text: We should add a single high-contrast skip link at the top of every page that only appears when focused, because this allows keyboard users to quickly bypass navigation and other repetitive elements, improving their overall experience. This decision prioritizes keyboard navigation over visual simplicity, accepting the trade-off that the link will take up some screen space when focused. By doing so, we ensure that users who rely on keyboard navigation can efficiently access the main content of the page. This approach also aligns with the principle of making the interface accessible to everyone, including those with mobility or dexterity impairments.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is sighted keyboard users will ignore the skip link because it looks like a decorative element until focused—even if it’s high-contrast. A better alternative is a skip link that’s always visible but visually subtle (e.g., small, low-contrast text) so all users recognize its purpose without relying on focus states. Settle this by testing with both screen reader and sighted keyboard users to measure skip link usage rates.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is sighted keyboard users will still overlook the skip link if it’s too subtle, defeating its purpose. A better alternative is a skip link that’s always visible but visually distinct—like a small, high-contrast button—so it’s unmistakable without cluttering the page.
